_note: The 16 frozen corpus fixtures, pinned by SHA-256 over the file bytes. The corpus used to be REGENERATED before every gate run, and that is why the numbers were not reproducible: the baseline was recorded against a corpus built with Chromium 149, GitHub Actions ships Chromium 150, and c4_i18n came out a different document whose vertical drift went 0.15pt to 0.7pt -- a 5x move in a gated metric caused by nothing in this repository. The bytes now live in testkit/fixtures/ and the numbers describe them exactly. Re-freeze deliberately with corpus_manifest.py update, and re-record the gate baseline in the same commit. The generators are still exercised by tests/test_corpus_generation.py, which reports drift without gating on it.

01_whitepaper_market.pdf.why: cover band, callouts, bar chart, ruled tables -- the Claude-style whitepaper this project started from

02_research_paper.pdf.why: two-column academic layout with figures and a references list

03_tech_report_code.pdf.why: monospace code blocks inside flowing prose

04_exec_brief.pdf.why: dense one-page brief; its live-text coverage is a recorded shortfall

05_memo.pdf.why: the minimal case -- if this one moves, something fundamental moved

c1_whitepaper.pdf.why: rounded-corner stat cards (D4) and a full-bleed cover band

c2_paper2col.pdf.why: true multi-column sections, the case a naive reading order destroys

c3_tables.pdf.why: nested tables (D3) -- a recorded shortfall on both backends

c4_i18n.pdf.why: CJK, Arabic and Hebrew: script continua and RTL reordering

c5_graphics.pdf.why: gradient band with knocked-out white text; rasterised SVG chart

c6_long.pdf.why: long enough that a per-page offset compounds into a page count error

c7_code.pdf.why: leading indentation, which PDFium does not report and PyMuPDF synthesises

c8_toc_links.pdf.why: table of contents with tab leaders and internal hyperlinks

f1_fpdf_brief.pdf.why: core-14 fonts with no FontDescriptor -- the serif-flag case

l1_word_native.pdf.why: a PDF printed from a word processor: the round trip back to its own kind

r1_reportlab_report.pdf.why: a second ReportLab dialect written by a different generator than corpus/
